feedback.problem:
Suppose that a $3\times 3$ matrix $H$ is reduced to row echelon form using the following elementary row operations, applied in the order in which they appear:

$$
{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2{R}_{1},\,{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}-8{R}_{1}.
$$

Given that $H$ has the LU factorization $H=LU,$ then $L=$
feedback.worked_solution:
Applying ${R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+2\cdot {R}_{1}$ and then ${R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+(-8)\cdot {R}_{1}$ is equivalent to multiplying $H$ from the left by the following elementary matrices:

$$
{{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -8 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{E}_{2}}\cdot {{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{{E}_{1}}\cdot H=U
$$

Now, since ${E}_{2}{E}_{1}H=U,$ we can invert ${E}_{2}$ and ${E}_{1}$ to arrive at the desired LU factorization:

$$
\begin{aligned}{E}_{2}{E}_{1}H & =U \\ {E}_{1}H & ={E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ H & ={E}_{1}^{-1}{E}_{2}^{-1}U \\ H & ={[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ -8 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}^{-1}U \\ H & =([\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 8 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}])U \\ H & ={{[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ -2 & 1 & 0 \\ 8 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}]}_{⏟}}_{L}\cdot U\end{aligned}
$$
